A slow-burn survival horror / creepypasta set in late autumn as cold rain soaks a remote pine forest. When the outbreak hits and strange videos flood social media, Wesley Barlow and June Calder retreat to the hidden A-frame treehouse Wesley built years ago above a rushing creek, then turn it into a real shelter. This grounded audio story focuses on practical survival: wood heat, clean water, food planning, hygiene routines, quiet load runs to an old family house, and the hard rule of keeping the treehouse boring and off everyone’s list. The creek’s constant noise becomes cover, but the bigger danger isn’t always the infected. It’s the living—local “volunteer wardens” who set up checkpoints, make lists, and start demanding supplies and weapons in the name of safety. Expect tense, realistic decisions, tight isolation rules, and a procedural vibe where every step has a reason and every mistake has a cost.

What’s inside:
– Shelter-in-place decision, isolation rules, inventory basics
– Wood stove heat, water filtering, food storage, light discipline
– Quiet hunting with a crossbow, creek fishing, low-profile routines
– Human threat: local quarantine wardens and escalating “rules”
– A confrontation that turns noise into a magnet

What actually happens when the world's most advanced military faces a relentless biological swarm? The ultimate argument is always that the army would just shoot them. But this relies on a fundamental misunderstanding of modern warfare. Wars are won by logistics and secure supply lines, not just massive firepower. 🧟‍♂️

We break down the brutal math of urban combat and why conventional military doctrine completely collapses within 72 hours. From the failure of supply chains and civilian gridlock to melted rifle barrels and the myth of invulnerable heavy armor, we explore exactly how a massive force falls to an exponential threat. 🧠

Using simple, clean visuals and logistical diagrams, we map out the timeline of the collapse. More importantly, we discuss what this means for your personal survival strategy. You will learn why bugging in is critical, the dangers of centralized safe zones, and how to build a microscopic off-grid civilization. 🔦 Let’s walk through the military collapse calmly.
